issues.description: The proposal fails to mention the CFO's high-confidence skepticism of consulting engagements due to being burned by a previous vendor in 2023. Omitting this makes the proposal seem tone-deaf to a major executive concern.
issues.suggested_fix: Acknowledge the past vendor challenges in the Understanding section and emphasize how the proposed milestone-based, risk-mitigated governance model specifically protects Northwind from repeating that experience.

issues.description: The proposal omits the high-confidence fact that previous internal attempts to fix these exact workflow issues have failed twice. This is a critical piece of context that justifies the need for external expertise.
issues.suggested_fix: Mention the two past failed internal attempts when describing the operational friction to highlight the complexity of the problem and validate the proposed architectural approach.

issues.description: The proposal mentions the ELD mandate but misses the specific business risks of non-compliance (fines and potential loss of operating authority).
issues.suggested_fix: Explicitly state that missing the ELD compliance deadline could result in fines or loss of operating authority to underscore the strategic importance of the timeline.

issues.description: There is a typo in the Future-Proof Architecture bullet point: 'future core core platform transitions'.

risks: Deep executive misalignment on the budget cap, pilot timeline (Q3 vs Q4), and core platform strategy (SaaS vs workflow fix) poses a significant risk to project kickoff and success, even though correctly identified in Open Questions.
The 24-week timeline leaves very little buffer before the November ELD mandate, meaning any project delays could expose the client to severe regulatory consequences.
